experience: Walk through a dense cathedral of old cabbage palms to a secluded spring at the end of a woodland spur. This is the Shepherd Spring shown in the supplied St Marks screenshot. duration: Editorial estimate: half a day; allow roughly 3–4 hours for the approximately 6-mile Spring Creek trailhead loop and spring spur.
cost: No trailhead-specific entrance price established in this check.
access: Use the named Spring Creek Highway trailhead and the established Florida Trail route. FWS describes an alternative 5.4-mile outing from Wakulla Beach Road; the two trailheads are not interchangeable. Refuge hunts, wet trails and closures affect access. The user's screenshot shows damaged boards; present boardwalk condition is unverified.

conditions.summary: FWS trail guidance and Florida Springs Council route checked October 28. No current boardwalk inspection or confirmation of swimming permission.

water: A spring-viewing and wildlife hike. FWS notes alligator presence; this record does not designate a swimming area.
mobility: Several miles on uneven, potentially muddy paths, with a spring-side boardwalk whose current repair condition is unknown.

access: Free permit or reservation required before arrival. Stay limit: 14 days within any consecutive 30-day period (WMA rule); per-booking maximum not captured Derived, not read from the 2026-27 brochure (FWC brochure app errored): rule text says Choctawhatchee River WMA general gun is 'the first 58 days of Zone D antlered deer season'; with FWC's 2026-27 Zone D dates that is Nov 26-29, 2026 and Dec 12, 2026 - Feb 3, 2027. Camping is allowed with a District permit in designated campgrounds. Orange requirement not checked.

conditions.summary: NWFWMD closures page read 2026-11-12 lists only Fillingim Landing canoe launch (Perdido River) as closed; no Hurricane Isaias closure posted for this site.
